mission_1.search: On the open map, BFS and A* both found a path of 13.5 meters. With that being said, BFS expanded 928 nodes, while A* expended only 700 nodes meaning that A* examined fewer cells. In my BFS code, I used a FIFO queue, which explores cells in the order they were added. In A*, I used a priority queue and the heuristic to prioritize cells with the lower estimated total cost. This is what helped A* find the shorts path while having to explore fewer cells.
mission_1.failure: On the constrained map, BFS found a path of 24.5 meters, while DFS found a longer path of 50 meters. This happened because my DFS implementation uses a stack and explores one path deeply before trying other paths, so it doesn't guarantee the shortest path. IDDFS reached the resource limit after 250,001 expansions because it repeatedly searches with increasing depth limits. On the unreachable map, all four algorithms returned no_path which means that they finished searching and didn't find any possible route. This is different from resource_limit which means that the search stopped because it ran out of time or expansions. It doesn't mean that the path doesn't exist. I used AI to help me write part of the code for IDDFS and A*. I worked thought the logic myself, wrote parts of the algorithms myself, and checked my implementations using the provided tests and evaluation results.
